title: Keep knowledge warm by using it
statement: Keep earlier knowledge alive by making later lessons need it, and send to separate spaced review only what nothing later can honestly use.
detail: The curriculum architecture BrainLift argues that knowledge kept warm by isolated spaced practice costs time and stays compartmentalised, and that a platform should not compensate for a poorly connected curriculum by drilling everything forever (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback2/WF - Curriculum Architecture Br - 260713-123107.md`). The reading project's practice spec adopted the theme sequence as the first spaced-practice system, with separate review as the backstop that keeps warm exactly the residue the sequence cannot honestly recruit downstream, and it treats the size of that residue as a design metric (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`). Knowledge kept warm this way is recalled through use rather than recognised, and the separate review is mixed across units.
against: The ledger is a draft planning map, not approved curriculum (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0147-draft-grade-3-science-ledger.qmd`).
